answer: Cross-Epoch Echo Consistency. Each identity must reproduce a hidden behavioural quill—a signed trace of its past actions—at the start of every epoch; the agent's new work must echo that trace within a tolerance. An identity failing the echo is isolated to an island of reduced trust until it re-earns consistency over several epochs. Splitting into sybils multiplies the trace-reproduction burden per copy, so an attacker pays full computational and latency cost for every fake identity, not one shared cost.
